```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(scales)
library(ggtext)
library(ggrepel)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
```

```{r globals}
# --- File path -------------------------------------------------------------
# Path to the compiled data file (sourced from DBM publications).
data_path <- "../data/Compiled_-_DPWH.xlsx"

# --- Which series to deflate by --------------------------------------------
# Either "CPI" or "GDPDeflator" (both indexed to 2018 = 100).
deflator_choice <- "CPI"

# --- Colours ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Fixed mapping so NEP/GAA/Actuals are consistent across every plot.
item_levels <- c("NEP", "GAA", "Actual Obligations")
item_colors <- c("NEP" = "#ffa6b0", "GAA" = "#3994fc", "Actual Obligations" = "#bcbef2")

# --- DPWH programs (consistent labelling began with the 2018 budget) -------
dpwh_programs <- c("General Administration and Support", "Support to Operations",
                   "Asset Preservation Program", "Network Development Program",
                   "Bridge Program", "Flood Management Program",
                   "Local Program", "Convergence and Special Support Program")

# Eight-colour palette built around the house three (#bcbef2 / #ffa6b0 / #3994fc):
# cool tones for the engineering programs, warm tones for the discretionary ones.
program_colors <- c(
  "General Administration and Support"      = "#bcbef2",  # periwinkle (house)
  "Support to Operations"                   = "#c8a8e9",  # soft violet
  "Asset Preservation Program"              = "#3994fc",  # blue (house)
  "Network Development Program"             = "#6fcfd6",  # teal
  "Bridge Program"                          = "#8fd9a8",  # mint
  "Flood Management Program"                = "#ffe27a",  # warm yellow
  "Local Program"                           = "#ffcf8b",  # apricot
  "Convergence and Special Support Program" = "#ffa6b0"   # salmon (house)
)

# --- Philippine Congresses (for reference lines) ---------------------------
# Short ordinal labels so they don't crowd the 1988-2026 span.
congresses_ph2 <- tibble(
  Congress = c("8th", "9th", "10th", "11th", "12th", "13th", "14th",
               "15th", "16th", "17th", "18th", "19th", "20th"),
  Congress_Start = as.Date(c("1987-07-27", "1992-07-27", "1995-07-24", "1998-07-27",
                             "2001-07-23", "2004-07-26", "2007-07-23", "2010-07-26",
                             "2013-07-22", "2016-07-25", "2019-07-22", "2022-07-25",
                             "2025-07-28"))
)

# --- Presidential administrations (inauguration dates) ---------------------
administrations_ph <- tibble(
  President = c("C. Aquino", "Ramos", "Estrada", "Arroyo",
                "B. Aquino III", "Duterte", "Marcos Jr."),
  Start = as.Date(c("1986-02-25", "1992-06-30", "1998-06-30", "2001-01-20",
                    "2010-06-30", "2016-06-30", "2022-06-30"))
)

# Clamp the first era to the left edge of the data so its label stays on-canvas,
# and only draw boundary lines that fall inside the plotted range.
data_start      <- as.Date("1988-01-01")
admin_labels    <- administrations_ph %>% mutate(LabelX = pmax(Start, data_start))
admin_lines     <- administrations_ph %>% filter(Start >= data_start)
congress_labels <- congresses_ph2     %>% mutate(LabelX = pmax(Congress_Start, data_start))
congress_lines  <- congresses_ph2     %>% filter(Congress_Start >= data_start)

# --- Shared x-axis: tick + label ONLY the first budget year of each Congress
# (FY1988 = 8th, FY1993 = 9th, ... FY2020 = 18th, FY2023 = 19th, FY2026 = 20th)
congress_first_fy <- as.Date(c("1988-01-01", "1993-01-01", "1996-01-01", "1999-01-01",
                               "2002-01-01", "2005-01-01", "2008-01-01", "2011-01-01",
                               "2014-01-01", "2017-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2023-01-01",
                               "2026-01-01"))
```

# Executive Summary: Warning Signs Before the Scandal

The 2025 flood-control scandal changed how the public reads the DPWH budget. It did not
create the budgetary warning signs. The appropriation records show that the conditions
that warranted a closer look appeared years before the scandal broke, from the middle of
the Duterte administration onward. This report reconstructs what a careful reader of the
NEP and GAA could already have seen, and then asks whether the FY 2027 budget departs from
that history or repeats it.

Three patterns recur across the period.

The first is large and recurrent change between what the Executive proposed and what
Congress enacted, concentrated in district engineering offices. In FY2019 the distance
between the proposal, the legislated bill, and the final GAA ran to tens of billions, and
the ₱95.4B presidential veto that followed showed how much the budget could shift between
stages. Across FY2017-2026 the district offices were adjusted every year, and in several
years the gross reshuffling among them was several times the net change the department
totals report.

The second is a classification break in FY2022. District-type local roads, multipurpose
buildings, and flood-control works that had sat in the Local Program moved into the
Convergence and Special Support Program, under the SIPAG and BIP labels. The program names
changed faster than the works did, so a comparison by program title understates how long
these activities have been funded.

The third is geographic concentration. The home districts of most presidents, Speakers,
and appropriations chairs were funded more generously while those officials held power,
though with clear exceptions. This is an association, not a finding of misconduct, and it
needs project-level evidence to carry more weight than that.

The scandal's budgetary echo is FY2026. Flood Management fell from about ₱251B proposed to
₱4.8B enacted, but most of that reduction was the Executive's own revised NEP, not a
congressional cut, and the flood-control total across all programs should be checked before
the reduction is read as a complete withdrawal of flood-control funding.

FY2027 is the test. At the House stage (HB 10858, as approved on second reading), the bill makes the
same shift from the Central Office to the districts that the enacted budgets have made every
year, lifting the district share of the department from 20% to 28%. It is not a final
appropriation, and on the evidence here it reproduces the earlier pattern rather than
breaking from it.

What this establishes, and what it does not: the budget record can show concentrations,
budget-stage anomalies, and label changes that deserved examination sooner than 2025. It
cannot, on its own, show that any earlier appropriation funded a ghost project, a kickback,
or a political favour. Those are separate questions that need audit, procurement, and
project-level records. A retrospectively recognisable red flag is a reason to demand
transparency, not a verdict of corruption.

A note on the figures. Unless stated otherwise, amounts are New Appropriations for the DPWH
Office of the Secretary, by operating unit, in nominal pesos. The long-run series in the
next section also includes Automatic Appropriations, so its totals run slightly higher, and
the share-of-national-budget figure uses that wider base. FY2019 and FY2025 GAA figures are
post-veto. FY2027 figures are the House second-reading stage, not an enacted GAA. Every
chart states its basis.

# Overview, Data, and Interpretation

This first section profiles the long-run budget of the **DPWH Office of the
Secretary**: a (still incomplete) time series of the
**NEP**, **GAA**, and **Actual Obligations** running back to 1988. Three views
are shown - the **nominal** trend, the department's **share of the national
budget**, and the **real (inflation-adjusted)** trend in constant 2018 prices.

All figures throughout this document are drawn from the National Expenditure
Program (NEP), General Appropriations Act (GAA), and related budget documents
published by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM).

A few conventions:

- Amounts are reported in **thousand pesos**; everything below is
  rescaled to **PHP billions** (`/ 1e6`).
- The headline series is **New + Automatic Appropriations** (the full
  agency budget, including automatic items). This is also the numerator used
  for the share of the national budget.
- Points mark **years with observed data**; the connecting line is interpolated,
  so visible gaps flag where encoding is still pending.

## How to Read the Operating-Unit Geography

The budget assigns appropriations to DPWH **operating units**: the Central Office, the
Regional Offices, and the District Engineering Offices (DEOs). These are administrative
budget-recording units. They are not the legislative districts represented in Congress. A
DEO's name or service area can overlap with an electoral constituency, but the two do not
correspond one to one, and money recorded under the Central Office may fund works built far
outside Metro Manila. So the operating-unit analysis in this report is a distribution of
appropriations by recorded operating unit, not a full accounting of where infrastructure is
built or a direct measure of any legislator's influence. The political-geography
comparisons later are screening indicators for project-level investigation, not proof of
funding to a specific legislative district.

| What the data identify | What they can show | What they cannot establish on their own |
|---|---|---|
| DPWH Central Office | Appropriations recorded against a central unit | The physical location of the funded works |
| DPWH Regional Office | Appropriations assigned to a regional unit | A full province-by-province distribution |
| DPWH District Engineering Office (DEO) | Appropriations recorded against a named field office | A one-to-one amount for a congressional district or a named lawmaker |
| PAP or project line, where detailed | The budgeted project classification, sometimes with location detail | Completion, contractor, disbursement, or beneficiary without other records |

## Program Classification: PREXC and the 2014-2017 Crosswalk

The program and sub-program series runs from FY2014, but it crosses a change in budget
architecture at FY2018. Beginning with the FY2018 budget, the NEP and GAA adopted the
Program Expenditure Classification (PREXC), supported by changes to the Unified Accounts
Code Structure (UACS). PREXC organises an agency's operations into programs and
sub-programs, with activities and projects recorded beneath them. Before FY2018 the DPWH
budget used a Major Final Output (MFO) structure, which does not line up one to one with
the PREXC programs.

To run Sections 4 and 5 back to 2014, the FY2014-2017 items are mapped onto the eight PREXC
programs by a crosswalk: road works split into Asset Preservation, Network Development
(including road upgrading), and the Bridge Program; flood works to Flood Management; the
MFO 3 access roads to Convergence and Special Support; locally-funded projects to the Local
Program; and foreign-assisted works distributed by type into the matching programs, since
PREXC folds foreign assistance into programs rather than holding it as a separate line. The
harmonized FY2014-2017 program totals reconcile to the operating-unit totals in Section 6
within about half a percent.

This is consistency of the reporting framework, not a guarantee that each category means the
same thing every year. The FY2022 move of Local Program activities into Convergence, SIPAG
and BIP is the clearest break within the PREXC period itself, and it has to be read by
project type, not by program name alone. The pre-2018 program labels are ours: we matched
the MFO structure onto the PREXC programs as closely as the two allow. Read them as a
defensible reconstruction for continuity, not as identical PREXC accounting. (UACS predates 2018 and
was modified for PREXC, not introduced then.)

## Budget Stages and Scope

Four distinctions run through the report, and the figures are labelled against them. The
**NEP** is the Executive's proposal and the **GAA** is the enacted law; for FY2026 the
Executive also issued a revised NEP (an errata), and for FY2027 the latest stage shown is
the House-stage budget (HB 10858, as approved on second reading), which is not an enacted
GAA. The FY2019 and FY2025 GAA figures are post-veto. The headline long-run series is New
plus Automatic Appropriations, while the program and operating-unit sections use New
Appropriations only, so those totals run slightly below the headline. The same fiscal
year can therefore carry two figures: the FY2019 proposal is ₱555.7B on the headline
basis but ₱544.5B in New Appropriations, and the FY2026 enacted budget is ₱530.9B
versus ₱529.6B. The gap is the automatic appropriations, and it is not a discrepancy. That New
Appropriations series now runs back to 2005, and the gap stays small throughout, between
about ₱1B and ₱11B a year. A recorded operating
unit is not the same as where a project is built or the legislative district a lawmaker
represents. And the difference between a proposal and the enacted law, the net NEP-to-GAA
change, is not by itself a congressional addition: where a veto or a revised NEP sits
between the two, the change belongs to that documented stage, not to Congress.

```{r load-data}
# New + Automatic Appropriations (the headline DPWH OSec budget)
dpwh_newauto <- read_xlsx(data_path, sheet = "DPWH_OSec", range = "A2:D41") %>%
  rename(FY = 1, NEP = 2, GAA = 3, `Actual Obligations` = 4)

# Total national budget (denominator for DPWH's share)
total_budget <- read_xlsx(data_path, sheet = "DPWH_OSec", range = "K2:N41") %>%
  rename(FY = 1, NEP = 2, GAA = 3, `Actual Obligations` = 4)

# Price indices (2018 = 100)
price_index <- read_xlsx(data_path, sheet = "DPWH_OSec", range = "U2:W41") %>%
  rename(FY = 1, CPI = 2, GDPDeflator = 3)

# Tidy long table with nominal, real, and share columns
dpwh_long <- dpwh_newauto %>%
  pivot_longer(-FY, names_to = "Item", values_to = "Amount") %>%
  left_join(
    total_budget %>% pivot_longer(-FY, names_to = "Item", values_to = "TotalBudget"),
    by = c("FY", "Item")
  ) %>%
  left_join(price_index, by = "FY") %>%
  mutate(
    FY_date  = as_date(str_c(FY, "-01-01")),
    Item     = factor(Item, levels = item_levels),
    AmountB  = Amount / 1e6,                       # thousand pesos -> PHP billions
    Deflator = .data[[deflator_choice]],
    RealB    = AmountB / (Deflator / 100),         # constant 2018 prices
    Share    = Amount / TotalBudget
  )

# DPWH New Appropriations only (the basis the program and district sections use),
# now compiled as a long series back to FY2005. Enacted (GAA) side only, for the
# nominal chart overlay; it tracks the New + Automatic series within a few billion.
newonly_gaa <- read_xlsx(data_path, sheet = "DPWH_OSec", range = "F2:I41") %>%
  setNames(c("FY", "NEP", "GAA", "Actual Obligations")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(GAA)) %>%
  transmute(FY_date = as_date(str_c(FY, "-01-01")),
            Item = "New Appropriations only (GAA)", AmountB = GAA / 1e6)
```

# The Long View: DPWH Appropriations Since 1988

The four views below track the DPWH Office of the Secretary's budget across nearly
four decades - in nominal pesos, as a share of the national budget, in
inflation-adjusted terms, and in a single reference table - before the rest of
the document turns to the program, item, and district-level detail of recent years.

## Nominal Trend

```{r plot-nominal}
nominal_data <- bind_rows(
  dpwh_long %>% filter(!is.na(AmountB)) %>% transmute(FY_date, Item = as.character(Item), AmountB),
  newonly_gaa %>% transmute(FY_date, Item, AmountB)
) %>% mutate(Item = factor(Item, levels = c(item_levels, "New Appropriations only (GAA)")))

ggplot(data = nominal_data) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_vline(data = admin_lines, aes(xintercept = Start),
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_vline(data = congress_lines, aes(xintercept = Congress_Start), alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_text(data = admin_labels, aes(x = LabelX, y = Inf, label = President),
            size = 2.4, fontface = "bold", hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = congress_labels, aes(x = LabelX, y = Inf, label = Congress),
            size = 1.9, color = "gray55", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 2.9) +
  geom_path(aes(x = FY_date, y = AmountB, color = Item), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = FY_date, y = AmountB, color = Item), size = 1.1) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "FY '%y", breaks = congress_first_fy, minor_breaks = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(item_colors, "New Appropriations only (GAA)" = "#4d4d4d")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PHP billions", color = NULL,
       title = "DPWH Office of the Secretary: New + Automatic, and New Appropriations",
       caption = "**Data Sources:** NEP and GAA documents; New + Automatic 1988-2026, New Appropriations only 2005-2026.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.15, 0.7),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
```

The dark line is the **New Appropriations** series, the basis the program and district
sections of this report use, now compiled back to FY2005. It runs just below the New +
Automatic headline, by a few billion a year, so the two bases tell the same long-run story:
a budget that climbs steeply from the mid-2010s. Two
deviations from the usual NEP-to-GAA pattern stand out, and both belong in
hearings: the **2019 GAA fell below the NEP** (the year of the ₱95.4B line-item veto; a smaller ₱26.1B veto also trimmed the 2025 GAA),
and the **2026 GAA drops sharply below its NEP** - the reverse of the
usual upward realignment seen in most other years.

## Share of the National Budget

```{r plot-share}
ggplot(data = dpwh_long %>% filter(!is.na(Share))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_vline(data = admin_lines, aes(xintercept = Start),
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_vline(data = congress_lines, aes(xintercept = Congress_Start), alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_text(data = admin_labels, aes(x = LabelX, y = Inf, label = President),
            size = 2.4, fontface = "bold", hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = congress_labels, aes(x = LabelX, y = Inf, label = Congress),
            size = 1.9, color = "gray55", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 2.9) +
  geom_path(aes(x = FY_date, y = Share, color = Item), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = FY_date, y = Share, color = Item), size = 1.1) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "FY '%y", breaks = congress_first_fy, minor_breaks = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = item_colors) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of Total Appropriations", color = NULL,
       title = "DPWH Office of the Secretary, as a Share of the National Budget",
       caption = "**Data Sources:** NEP and GAA documents, 1988-2026.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.13, 0.55),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
```

The share view rescales the same money against the size of the whole budget.
The department's footprint roughly **doubles from ~6-8% (1990s-2000s) to a
mid-teens share** in the latest years - evidence that DPWH's expansion outpaced
overall budget growth, not merely tracked it. The 2026 NEP-to-GAA gap reappears
here as a one-year contraction in the GAA share.

## Real Trend (Inflation-Adjusted)

```{r plot-real}
ggplot(data = dpwh_long %>% filter(!is.na(RealB))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_vline(data = admin_lines, aes(xintercept = Start),
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_vline(data = congress_lines, aes(xintercept = Congress_Start), alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_text(data = admin_labels, aes(x = LabelX, y = Inf, label = President),
            size = 2.4, fontface = "bold", hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = congress_labels, aes(x = LabelX, y = Inf, label = Congress),
            size = 1.9, color = "gray55", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 2.9) +
  geom_path(aes(x = FY_date, y = RealB, color = Item), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = FY_date, y = RealB, color = Item), size = 1.1) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "FY '%y", breaks = congress_first_fy, minor_breaks = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = item_colors) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PHP billions (constant 2018 prices)", color = NULL,
       title = "DPWH Office of the Secretary, in Real Terms",
       subtitle = str_c("Deflated by the ",
                        if_else(deflator_choice == "CPI", "CPI", "GDP deflator"),
                        " (2018 = 100)"),
       caption = "**Data Sources:** NEP and GAA documents, 1988-2026; PSA price indices.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.15, 0.7),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
```

Holding prices constant at 2018 tempers the nominal story: much of the post-2018
"growth" is the price level catching up. In real terms the GAA budget is
**broadly flat between 2018 and 2023** before resuming its climb - a useful
counterweight to headline peso figures in the hearing room. (Figures here use the
CPI as the price base; the GDP-deflator version tells the same story.)

## Summary Table

```{r summary-table}
dpwh_table <- dpwh_long %>%
  mutate(code = recode(Item, "NEP" = "NEP", "GAA" = "GAA",
                       "Actual Obligations" = "AO")) %>%
  select(FY, code, AmountB, RealB, Share) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = code, values_from = c(AmountB, RealB, Share)) %>%
  transmute(
    `FY`                   = FY,
    `NEP`                  = AmountB_NEP,
    `GAA`                  = AmountB_GAA,
    `Actual Oblig.`        = AmountB_AO,
    `Realignment (GAA-NEP)`  = AmountB_GAA - AmountB_NEP,
    `DPWH Share (GAA)`     = Share_GAA,
    `GAA, real 2018`       = RealB_GAA
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(FY))

# Pre-format so blanks read as "-" rather than NA
fmt_b <- function(x) { xn <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)); ifelse(is.na(xn), "--", comma(xn, accuracy = 0.1)) }

dpwh_table %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(NEP, GAA, `Actual Oblig.`, `Realignment (GAA-NEP)`, `GAA, real 2018`), fmt_b),
    `DPWH Share (GAA)` = ifelse(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`DPWH Share (GAA)`))), "--",
                                percent(`DPWH Share (GAA)`, accuracy = 0.1))
  ) %>%
  kbl(align = "lrrrrrr", escape = FALSE,
      caption = "DPWH Office of the Secretary, New + Automatic Appropriations (PHP billions unless noted)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 13)
```

## A Warning-Sign Timeline

Before the detail, here is the sequence the rest of the report documents, and how to read
each step. The patterns are observable in the appropriation record; the right-hand column
is what they do and do not support.

| Period | Observable pattern in this report | How to read it |
|---|---|---|
| **FY2014–2016** | The district-oriented Local Program already climbing and the enacted budget already running above the proposal, with road and flood works dominant (pre-PREXC labels matched to the PREXC programs as best we could) | The baseline the later shifts build on, not yet remarkable on its own |
| **FY2017–2019** | Large NEP-to-GAA adjustments, and the extraordinary FY2019 veto | An early sign that budget-stage changes deserved item-level review, not proof of a scheme |
| **FY2020–2022** | Recurring DEO-coded increases; the Local Program gives way to Convergence, SIPAG and BIP | Administrative reallocation persists, and a comparability break appears |
| **FY2023–2025** | Convergence peaks; large district-office concentrations; the 2025 flood-control scandal breaks | The patterns were already large before the scandal exposed them |
| **FY2026** | Flood Management cut sharply, most of it in the Executive's revised NEP | A budgetary response, with most of the reduction made before Congress acted |
| **FY2027 (House stage)** | The Central-Office-to-district shift repeats; district share rises 20% to 28% | The test of whether practice has changed; on this evidence it repeats |

# The DPWH Budget by Program

DPWH organises its budget into eight **programs**. PREXC program labelling begins
with the **2018 budget**; the **2014-2017** figures here are matched from the
earlier MFO-based structure onto the PREXC programs, as closely as we could, by a documented
crosswalk (see the data note in Section 2),
so this section now runs **2014-2026**. Amounts are in pesos, rescaled to **PHP
billions**. All figures are **New Appropriations**, and the harmonized program totals
reconcile to the operating-unit totals in Section 6 within about half a percent.

```{r load-byprogram}
# 2018-2027 program totals: the compiled PREXC program breakdown.
byprogram_18 <- read_xlsx(data_path, sheet = "NewAppro_ByProgram") %>%
  transmute(FY = as.integer(FY), Program, NEP, GAA,
            Vetoed = replace_na(as.numeric(Vetoed), 0))

# 2014-2017 program totals, harmonized from the pre-PREXC (MFO-based) encoding.
# The 2014-2017 budget used Major Final Outputs, not PREXC programs, so each leaf
# item is mapped to one of the eight PREXC programs by the crosswalk below and
# summed. Road works split into Asset Preservation / Network Development / Bridge,
# flood works to Flood Management, MFO 3 access roads to Convergence, locally-funded
# projects to the Local Program, and foreign-assisted works are distributed by type.
# See the data note in Section 2. GenAdmin and Support to Operations carry over.
prexc_xwalk_1417 <- function(L1, L2, L3) dplyr::case_when(
  str_detect(L2, "Assets Preservation") ~ "Asset Preservation Program",
  str_detect(L2, "Network Development") | str_detect(L2, "Road Upgrading") ~ "Network Development Program",
  str_detect(L1, "MFO 1") & str_detect(L2, "Bridges") ~ "Bridge Program",
  str_detect(L1, "MFO 2") ~ "Flood Management Program",
  str_detect(L1, "MFO 3") ~ "Convergence and Special Support Program",
  str_detect(L1, "Locally-Funded") ~ "Local Program",
  str_detect(L1, "Foreign-Assisted") & str_detect(L2, "Flood") ~ "Flood Management Program",
  str_detect(L1, "Foreign-Assisted") & str_detect(L3, "Bridge") ~ "Bridge Program",
  str_detect(L1, "Foreign-Assisted") ~ "Network Development Program",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_)

.raw1417 <- read_xlsx(data_path, sheet = "2014-2017", col_names = FALSE)
.h <- as.character(unlist(.raw1417[1, ])); .h[1:4] <- c("L0", "L1", "L2", "L3")
.h[is.na(.h)] <- paste0("x", which(is.na(.h))); names(.raw1417) <- make.unique(.h)
.pre1417 <- .raw1417[-1, ] %>% mutate(across(c(L0, L1, L2, L3), as.character))
.long1417 <- function(df) df %>%
  pivot_longer(matches("^(NEP|GAA_)[0-9]{4}_Amount$"), names_to = "key", values_to = "amt") %>%
  mutate(FY = as.integer(str_extract(key, "[0-9]{4}")),
         stage = if_else(str_detect(key, "^NEP"), "NEP", "GAA"),
         amt = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(amt))) %>%
  group_by(Program, FY, stage) %>% summarise(amt = sum(amt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stage, values_from = amt)
# Operations programs from the leaf (L3) rows
.d1417 <- .pre1417; .d1417$L3o <- .d1417$L3
.d1417 <- .d1417 %>% fill(L0, L1, L2, .direction = "down")
.ops1417 <- .d1417 %>% filter(!is.na(L3o)) %>%
  mutate(Program = prexc_xwalk_1417(L1, L2, L3)) %>% filter(!is.na(Program)) %>% .long1417()
# GenAdmin + Support to Operations from their L0 total rows (before fill)
.oh1417 <- .pre1417 %>%
  filter(L0 %in% c("GENERAL ADMINISTRATION AND SUPPORT", "SUPPORT TO OPERATIONS")) %>%
  mutate(Program = recode(L0,
    "GENERAL ADMINISTRATION AND SUPPORT" = "General Administration and Support",
    "SUPPORT TO OPERATIONS" = "Support to Operations")) %>% .long1417()
byprogram_14 <- bind_rows(.ops1417, .oh1417) %>% mutate(Vetoed = 0)

byprogram <- bind_rows(byprogram_14, byprogram_18) %>%
  mutate(Program = factor(Program, levels = dpwh_programs),
         NEP_B = NEP / 1e9, GAA_B = GAA / 1e9,  # GAA is final (post-veto)
         Veto_B = Vetoed / 1e9, Realign = (GAA - NEP) / 1e9) %>%
  arrange(FY, Program)

# Substantive programs (drops the two overhead lines) for the NEP-vs-GAA panels
substantive <- setdiff(dpwh_programs,
                       c("General Administration and Support", "Support to Operations"))
```
